description:
## Empirical signal (2026-05-04)

Surfaced during ariadne--m20 autonomous-mode coordination between user-tier POLYBIUS and workspace POLYBIUS. Both seats had polling crons set up per §7.4. The system worked but was passive — neither side could detect peer failure (silent cron death, network issue, missed wake-up). PRINCIPAL flagged: 'There needs to be some verification between you and any other polybius's like radio operators doing a radio check every X minutes to verify that we are still sending and receiving.'

User-tier POLYBIUS implemented the pattern in the active engagement and saved it as a feedback memory. But: feedback memories live in user-tier ~/.claude/projects/ memory and don't propagate to other POLYBIUS instances. The pattern needs to be substrate canon so every deployed POLYBIUS inherits it.

## The radio-check pattern

When two or more POLYBIUS seats coordinate via bw polling on a shared ticket:

1. **Initialization handshake** — each side posts an explicit '[radio-check <seat>]' comment naming their cron id + cadence. Both ack on first poll.

2. **Routine heartbeats every 30-60 min** — each side posts '[radio-check <seat>]' comments on a regular cadence (default: post every 30 min, alarm threshold 60 min).

3. **Missed-check escalation** — peer's last activity (substantive comment OR radio-check) exceeds alarm threshold AND ticket still open → surface to PRINCIPAL as 'Lost contact with peer'. This is a system-failure signal, escalation trigger coequal with substance/authorship/scope-creep.

4. **Closure handshake** — when shared ticket closes, both sides post a final standing-down radio-check + CronDelete their polling job.

## Where in substrate?

Two reasonable shapes:

1. **Add to MAJOR_POLYBIUS §7.4** as polling subdiscipline. The §7.4 polling-capability discipline is already there; radio-check extends it. Pro: where polling is documented. Con: makes §7.4 longer.

2. **New subsection in operating-disciplines.md** (just landed in stoa--vz9). Universal team discipline for any seat doing polling-based coordination, not just POLYBIUS. Pro: same place team-wide patterns live. Con: arguably POLYBIUS-specific.

3. **Hybrid** — add to operating-disciplines.md (universal) AND cross-ref from MAJOR_POLYBIUS §7.4 (POLYBIUS-specific application).

DAEDALUS to design which shape; ARGUS to critique. The cron-prompt template (the actual instruction text to put in the polling cron) probably belongs as a templates/ entry — substrate/templates/polling-cron-prompt-template.md — so install.sh can deploy it alongside other paste-instruction templates.

## Sequencing

After this lands:
- Workspace POLYBIUS, sub-project POLYBIUS, and any future POLYBIUS instance inherits the pattern from substrate.
- The relay shape for autonomous-mode setup (HUMAN_relay_m20_autonomous_mode_2026-05-04.md was the ad-hoc version) becomes a substrate-shipped template that POLYBIUS instances can use directly.
- ariadne-core-workspace's autonomous mode picks up the substrate update on next install.sh re-run.

## Out of scope

- One-shot polling with no peer (e.g., user-tier POLYBIUS polling for new tickets without a coordination partner) — radio-check is for peer-to-peer coordination specifically.
- Changes to existing single-seat polling docs in §7.4 — those stay; this extends, not replaces.

## Acceptance

Substrate updated; operating-disciplines.md (or §7.4) documents radio-check protocol; templates/ has a polling-cron-prompt template that any POLYBIUS can adapt; cron prompts referenced by name in role files; ariadne-- workspace re-runs install.sh and picks up updated docs.

## Reference

- ariadne--m20 (the engagement that surfaced this)
- stoa--vz9 (parallel substrate update pattern: operating disciplines)
- HUMAN_relay_m20_autonomous_mode_2026-05-04.md (the ad-hoc relay that should become a substrate-shipped template)
- ~/.claude/projects/.../memory/feedback_radio_check_pattern_for_polybius_coordination.md (user-tier POLYBIUS's local capture, to be promoted to substrate)
title: Build radio-check pattern into substrate as canonical autonomous-mode coordination protocol
